title: Lesson 29 - LWC Embeds and Custom/Standard Components in OmniScripts
description: Advise on leveraging LWC (Lightning Web Component) Embeds and Custom/Standard Components within Omniscripts, including Child Omniscripts for reuse, or Flexcards to enhance the user experience and maintain corporate branding.

questions.question: An OmniScript needs a custom map picker that standard elements cannot provide. What is the appropriate approach?
options: Add an LWC Embed that renders the custom map picker and writes the selection to the data JSON
Add a text Input for the location
questions.explanation: When a standard element cannot express the interaction, an LWC Embed is the right tool: it renders the custom component and writes the result to the data JSON. A standard picklist or text input cannot provide a map picker, and a FlexCard is a display component, not an input.

questions.question: A consultant is deciding whether to build a custom LWC or use a standard element for a simple picklist. What is the better choice?
options: Build the custom LWC for more control
Use the standard picklist, since it already solves the interaction with less cost
questions.explanation: Standard components should be the default because they cover most needs with less build, test, and maintenance cost. A custom LWC is warranted only when a standard element cannot do the job. A FlexCard is display, and a Formula computes a value.

questions.question: An LWC Embed in an OmniScript writes its result to the data JSON under a name that does not match what the save logic expects. What is the result?
options: The save logic reads the correct value automatically
The value is stored but the save logic reads a different or empty value, so the data is lost or wrong
questions.explanation: The data JSON name is the contract. If the LWC writes under a name the save logic does not expect, the save reads a different or empty value and the data is lost or wrong. The contract must be agreed and matched before building.
